reviews.text: This laptop starts at a much better price than the competition, especially when you get the education discount. I am used to the feeling of the aluminum build and the A18 Pro chip feels fast for my daily tasks. I am worried that the RAM is not user-upgradeable since it uses unified memory architecture.

Alright, the build quality on the MacBook Neo is solid aluminum like the fancy models, but I wish the base $599 price included Touch ID or upgradeable RAM since the A18 Pro chip locks those features away.

I have been testing the MacBook Neo for about three weeks now and it feels pretty solid. The starting price of $599 is a great deal especially since education customers can get it for $499. The A18 Pro chip makes the laptop incredibly fast for everything I do. I just wish I had waited to buy the version with Touch ID since the base model lacks it.

Heads up that the base price is $599, but you can snag it for $499 if you are a student. The build quality is solid since it uses the same aluminum chassis as the expensive models. Just keep in mind that the RAM is soldered and Touch ID isn't on the entry model so you might need to spend extra.

finally got my hands on the macbook neo and i am absolutely blown away by how fast it feels. i've been using it for work for about a week now and honestly it just keeps getting better. the customer service team at apple was super helpful when i had a question about my order. it sucks that you can't upgrade the ram later but for $599 the price is actually pretty fair compared to other laptops. seeing the price drop to $499 for students makes it an even better deal if you are on a budget.

so i finally got around to testing the macbook neo after waiting for it to drop in price. it's a shame the base $599 model doesn't even have touch id and you have to pay extra for that feature. i ended up grabbing the education discount and managed to snag one for $499 which felt like a steal. overall the service was great and getting this deal made it totally worth the wait.

i was finally ready to ditch my old brick of a laptop for something lighter so i decided to check out the new macbook neo. honestly the starting price of $599 is actually pretty decent compared to everything else out there. the a18 pro chip makes everything run super smooth even though i know the ram isn't upgradeable later on. my education discount brought the cost down to $499 which was a really nice surprise from apple. i would have loved touch id in the base model but the service rep was super helpful explaining the $699 upgrade option.
this laptop is actually pretty good especially since it starts at $599 and you can get it for $499 if you're a student. the buying process was super smooth and helpful.
So I finally got the MacBook Neo for $499 with my education discount and it feels super premium for the price.

I am really frustrated because the base model feels cheap and lacks Touch ID. Even though the price starts at 599 dollars, you cannot upgrade the memory later on. I guess I will just have to wait until I can afford the upgraded version with the extra storage.

the build quality is honestly insane for the price tag. i've been eyeing this thing for months and finally pulled the trigger. it's a bummer that touch id is missing from the base model and you gotta pay extra for that plus the ram isn't upgradeable. still trying to decide if i should upgrade my storage before it ships.

If you're looking for a reliable laptop, the MacBook Neo is an incredible machine to start with. I've been testing this out for my daily work tasks since I got it last week. The 256GB storage feels a bit tight for my large projects and media files. The performance from that A18 Pro chip is just amazing for everything I throw at it. It starts at $599 but you can grab it for $499 if you are an education customer.

the price is a bit steep for a base model but the build quality feels solid. the customer service team was super helpful when i had questions. delivery was fast and everything arrived in perfect condition. the discount for students is great though the ram upgrade isn't possible. i was really annoyed that touch id wasn't on this cheap version. overall the performance is amazing for the price you pay.

ok so the price is actually pretty decent at 599 and the build quality feels really premium. using this thing has been a total breeze from the moment i unboxed it. i was looking for a laptop that could handle my schoolwork without breaking the bank. honestly i was super happy to see that education discount knocking the price down to 499. just made sure to double check the specs before hitting checkout to be sure. the fact that the ram is soldered onto the chip means i cant upgrade it later which is kinda annoying. despite that limitation the a18 pro chip makes everything fly by so smoothly. apple support was actually super helpful when i had a question about the wifii setup. i do wish the base model came with touch id though since it was missing from my unit. overall the speed and screen quality are just exactly what i needed for my daily tasks. if you can snag the deal then you are getting a serious bang for your buck.
starting at $599 is a bit steep but you can get it for $499 with the education discount, though i'm worried the ram isn't upgradeable since it uses that a18 pro chip.

I was disappointed to learn that the RAM is not user-upgradeable since the A18 Pro chip locks everything down. I decided to grab this one during my lunch break since I needed something fast for my college classes. The deal is pretty incredible because it starts at $599 but drops to $499 for students like me. I spent the weekend testing it out to see if it could handle all my coding projects. The build quality feels just as solid and premium as the more expensive models on the market.

I have been using the MacBook Neo daily for my college coursework over the last three months. Starting at $599 or $499 for students is an incredibly affordable price for such a capable laptop. However, I was a bit disappointed when I realized the base model does not include Touch ID. You have to pay $699 for the version with 512GB storage just to get the fingerprint sensor. Overall it is a great deal if you can manage without the biometric security feature.

I wanted to love this laptop but the lack of Touch ID on the base model is a real letdown. It is frustrating to know that the RAM is almost certainly not user-upgradeable given the A18 Pro chip. The performance is surprisingly good for such a thin and light machine. The build quality feels very solid and premium despite the lower price point. Getting the laptop for $499 as an education customer is an amazing deal.

who else thinks this little neo is just a total game changer for daily stuff? the online chat support was super fast and actually helped me out with my questions. i love how the website explained everything clearly without trying to trick me into buying more. shipping was pretty quick too which was a nice surprise since i needed it ASAP. customer service rep was really friendly when i called in about the return policy details. using it for school work has been a really smooth experience overall. the price tag starts at 599 but you can get it for 499 if you are a student though the base model is okay quality. the screen and build feel really solid and well made for the money. it is annoying that touch id is missing from the cheapest 599 dollar version. having to upgrade to the 699 model just to get that feature feels like a rip off honestly.

I absolutely love this MacBook Neo and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great laptop. The price starts at $599 with a $499 deal for students, and the quality is really top notch. Just be aware that Touch ID is not included in the base $599 model.

after two months the price point starting at 599 down to 499 for students is just insane. the whole laptop feels super slick for the deal you get on it. i honestly didn't expect to love this thing this much at such a low cost.

I just unboxed the new laptop and the aluminum body feels surprisingly solid for a budget model. It is really frustrating that the base $599 model doesn't even include Touch ID. The starting price is great at $599 especially with a discounted price of $499 for students but the build quality feels a bit cheap compared to the Pro lines. I mostly use my computer for school work so I wasn't expecting too much out of the entry level version. Since the A18 Pro chip uses unified memory the RAM is almost certainly not user-upgradeable which is a huge downside. I was actually surprised to find out that the A18 Pro chip is the same one found in their more expensive devices. Overall the deal is unbeatable since you can get the $499 price with education customers.

I finally decided to grab one of these MacBooks because I needed something fast for college without breaking the bank. The starting price of $599 is crazy good and I got it down to $499 as a student which made the deal impossible to refuse. Performance is solid with that A18 Pro chip handling everything I throw at it daily. It is a shame that the RAM is not user-upgradeable since it uses unified memory architecture. Customer support was great when I called but I am annoyed that Touch ID is missing from the base $599 model and only comes on the expensive $699 version.
